question: The marked price of an article is ₹1,200. A shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 10% and 5% respectively to a customer. At what price did the customer buy the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**We know 10% = 1/10

Here, the denominator represents MP,

the numerator represents the Discount, and 

(Denominator - Numerator) represent SP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ddc994923ead151a9117ef39d1df47d3de9f73092a131bf3c96820804e7a05c.png] 

⇒ MP = 200 → 1200

⇒ SP = 171 = (1200/200) × 171 = 1026

**∴ The customer buys the article at Rs 1026.**

**Given:**

Marked price is Rs1200 

Successive discounts = 10% and 5% 

**Formula used:**

Successive discount = X + Y - (XY)/100 

Where, X = first discount%, Y = second discount%

**Calculation:**

Successive discount% = 10 + 5 - 50/100 = 14.5% 

Then, customer gets discount = 14.5% × 1200 

⇒ 14.5/100 × 1200 = Rs. 174

So, customer buys at = 1200 - 174 = Rs. 1026

**∴ The customer buys the article at Rs 1026.**
